The expected stdout is correct, but it does not pin the documented determination. Lines 1-5 (EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT ... EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED) run with checking ENABLED. §14.6.13.1.3 5)/7) and the unnumbered paragraph after 8) then require EVERY conforming implementation to produce code and raise the condition at run time. Only unchecked fatal conditions get the no-code latitude. So these lines print the same whichever fatal ECs an implementation detects at compile time. The only latitude-dependent leg is OFF-CONTINUED. It cannot tell 'only EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED is compile-detected' apart from 'none is' or 'all are, as warnings'. It also passes for an implementation that detects the condition and omits only that statement's code. The one thing it separates is an implementation that refuses the whole compilation. It also mixes in §14.6.13.1.3 8), the separate implementor choice about continuing after an unchecked fatal EC. What A.1 69 documents is WHICH conditions are detected at compile time and WHEN. Its only observable is the COBOLNET1662 diagnostic, which the corpus runner does not compare (the same pattern as the misc-p2 DOC-A.1-16 overturn). Leave the row test-needed. Close it with a conformance-test/unit test instead: COBOLNET1662 PRESENT for an unavailable ORDER TABLE literal, and NO fatal-EC diagnostic for constant E(6), X(7:2), 1/0 and SQRT(-1).
